% ------------------------------- 1  Motivation & research questions ----------
\begin{panel}{1}{Motivation \& Research Questions}
  {\pbodys
   \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=8mm,itemsep=4mm,topsep=0mm,parsep=0pt]
     \item In a POMDP the optimal action depends on information that has left
           the observation. The remedy is a recurrent policy carrying a hidden
           state \mono{h} forward.
     \item The concession is to \textbf{truncate the backward pass to \Lw{}
           steps}, a value usually inherited in silence from whatever codebase
           one starts from.
     \item \mono{MiniGrid-MemoryS17Random-v0} makes that measurable: a cue seen
           only in the west room decides which prong of the T junction pays,
           and the 7\,\tx\,7 view makes both prongs identical.
     \item A \textbf{memoryless policy is capped at 0.5}, so the gap from 0.5
           to 1.0 is exactly the memory a run has acquired.
     \item One PPO pipeline stays fixed. Only the encoder changes: a memoryless
           MLP, or a GRU with \Lw{} in \{1,\,4,\,8,\,full BPTT\}.
   \end{itemize}\par}
  \vspace{6mm}

  \begin{callout}
    {\psmall\color{luhblue}
     \textbf{Research questions}\par
     \vspace{3mm}
     \textbf{Q1} How far back must the gradient reach? Carrying \mono{h}
     forward is free at any \Lw, so is a short window enough to \textbf{learn
     what to store}?\par
     \vspace{3mm}
     \textbf{Q2} What does that reach cost in time and in VRAM? A shorter
     window is intuitively cheaper; we check whether it is.\par}
  \end{callout}
  \vspace{7mm}

  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=165mm]{figures/task_memory_s17}
  \par\vspace{3mm}
  \RaggedRight
  {\pcap The cue sits in the west room; the agent spawns in the corridor
   facing away from it, so the information has to be sought out.\par}
\end{panel}

\panelgap

% ------------------------------------------------------------- 2  Approach ---
\begin{panel}{2}{Approach}
  \phead{Network}
  \centering
  \posterfig{200mm}{model_architecture_poster}
  \par\vspace{3mm}
  \RaggedRight
  {\pcap The encoder is the \textbf{only} difference between arms: an MLP, or a
   single GRU layer carrying \mono{h} forward.\par}
  \vspace{7mm}

  \phead{PPO objective}
  {\pbodys One iteration collects W\,=\,32 workers \tx{} T\,=\,361 steps and
   computes GAE advantages over the \textbf{whole} rollout, before any split,
   with returns $\hat{R}_t = \hat{A}_t + V(s_t)$:\par}
  {\pbodys
   \begin{gather*}
     \hat{A}_t = \delta_t + \gamma\lambda(1-d_t)\hat{A}_{t+1},
     \qquad \delta_t = r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1})(1-d_t) - V(s_t)
   \end{gather*}\par}
  {\pbodys Three shuffled epochs then minimise a clipped policy loss, a value
   loss and an entropy bonus, with
   $\rho_t = \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)/\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(a_t \mid s_t)$:\par}
  {\pbodys
   \begin{gather*}
     \mathcal{L}^{\pi} = -\,\mathbb{E}_t\big[\min\big(\rho_t \hat{A}_t,\;
       \mathrm{clip}(\rho_t, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon)\,\hat{A}_t\big)\big]\\
     \mathcal{L}^{V} = \mathbb{E}_t\big[(V_\theta(s_t) - \hat{R}_t)^2\big],
     \qquad
     \mathcal{L}^{H} = \mathbb{E}_t\big[\mathcal{H}(\pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t))\big]\\
     \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}^{\pi} + c_v\,\mathcal{L}^{V} - c_e\,\mathcal{L}^{H}
   \end{gather*}\par}
  {\pcap Every expectation covers real timesteps only: padding never enters the
   loss, and gradients are clipped before each Adam step.\par}
\end{panel}

\panelgap

% -------------------------------------------- 6  Limitations & future work ---
\begin{panel}{6}{Limitations \& Future Work}
  {\pbodys
   \textbf{One task, one architecture, one algorithm.} L \ensuremath{\in}
   \{5,\,6,\,7\} was never run, so the threshold is \textbf{bracketed, not
   located}, and five seeds separate 0.5 from 1.0 safely but support no finer
   claim.
   \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=8mm,itemsep=4mm,topsep=5mm,parsep=0pt]
     \item \textbf{Locate the threshold.} Sweep L \ensuremath{\in}
           \{5,\,6,\,7\} and set the corridor length directly instead of
           leaving it to the environment, a causal test of the gap account.
     \item \textbf{Add R2D2-style burn-in.} Does a short window then behave
           like a long one? If so the threshold is about optimisation, not the
           gradient path.
     \item \textbf{Repeat with an LSTM and a small transformer}, where the
           analogous knob is the attention window.
   \end{itemize}\par}
  \vspace{5mm}
  {\color{hairline}\rule{\linewidth}{0.8mm}}
  \vspace{3mm}
  {\ptiny \textbf{References.} Hausknecht \& Stone 2015 \textperiodcentered{}
   Kapturowski et al.\ 2019 (R2D2) \textperiodcentered{} Ni et al.\ 2022
   \textperiodcentered{} Schulman et al.\ 2017 (PPO) \textperiodcentered{}
   Chevalier-Boisvert et al.\ 2023 (MiniGrid)\par}
\end{panel}

\end{minipage}%

\begin{panel}{3}{Experiments \& Hyperparameter Optimization}
  \phead{The recurrent encoder}
  \centering
  \posterfig{210mm}{gru_cell}
  \par\vspace{3mm}
  \RaggedRight
  {\pcap A single GRU layer of tuned width. \Lw{} caps how far back the
   gradient may travel, never the forward pass.\par}
  \vspace{6mm}

  \phead{The five arms}
  \psmall
  \setlength{\tabcolsep}{0pt}
  \setlength{\heavyrulewidth}{1.0mm}
  \setlength{\lightrulewidth}{0.5mm}
  \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
  \begin{tabular}{@{}p{108mm}>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{72mm}%
                   >{\centering\arraybackslash}p{104mm}%
                   >{\centering\arraybackslash}p{96mm}%
                   >{\centering\arraybackslash}p{100mm}@{}}
    \arrayrulecolor{luhblue}\toprule
    \textbf{\textcolor{luhblue}{arm}} &
    \textbf{\textcolor{luhblue}{encoder}} &
    \textbf{\textcolor{luhblue}{gradient reach}} &
    \textbf{\textcolor{luhblue}{chunks per worker}} &
    \textbf{\textcolor{luhblue}{tuned hidden size}} \\
    \midrule
    MLP (baseline) & MLP & one step, no recurrence & n/a & 360 (2 layers) \\
    GRU, \Leq{1}   & GRU & 1 step        & 361 & 216 \\
    GRU, \Leq{4}   & GRU & 4 steps       &  91 & 360 \\
    \rowcolor{tintblue}
    GRU, \Leq{8}   & GRU & 8 steps       &  46 & 480 \\
    \rowcolor{tintblue}
    GRU, full BPTT & GRU & whole episode & episode cuts only & 280 \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \par\vspace{3mm}
  {\pcap Chunks per worker is \ensuremath{\lceil T/L \rceil}; episode
   boundaries cut further. Each chunk is seeded with the hidden state the
   rollout recorded there, so every GRU arm carries \textbf{identical
   information forward} and only the backward pass differs.\par}
  \vspace{7mm}

  \phead{Hyperparameter optimization}
  {\pbodys
   \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=8mm,itemsep=4mm,topsep=0mm,parsep=0pt]
     \item \textbf{Budget.} One Optuna study \textbf{per arm}: 50 TPE trials,
           sampler seeded at 42. Five studies \tx{} 50 trials \tx{} 5 seeds =
           \textbf{250 training runs}, \ensuremath{\approx}\,236 GPU-hours on
           one RTX 3060 Laptop (12\,GB).
     \item \textbf{Per trial.} The same five seeds [0,\,15,\,12,\,97,\,98] for
           1000 iterations of 32\,\tx\,361 steps
           (\ensuremath{\approx}\,11.6M env steps per seed), evaluated on 50
           fixed held-out mazes.
     \item \textbf{Space.} Nine parameters over \textbf{identical} ranges for
           both encoders (\mono{lr}, \mono{gamma}, \mono{gae\_lambda},
           \mono{clip\_eps}, \mono{entropy\_coef}, \mono{value\_coef},
           \mono{wd}, \mono{max\_grad\_norm}, \mono{hidden\_size}), plus MLP
           depth. Nothing that buys compute is searchable, and \Lw{} is fixed
           per study.
   \end{itemize}\par}
  \vspace{4mm}
  {\pbodys \textbf{Objective.} Evaluation return over the five seeds, the
   mean penalised by the spread across them:\par}
  {\pbodys
   \begin{equation*}
     \mathrm{score} = \mathrm{mean}_s\big[\text{return}_s\big]
                    - \mathrm{std}_s\big[\text{return}_s\big]
   \end{equation*}\par}
  {\pcap A trial excellent on two seeds and broken on three loses to one that
   is merely good on all five.\par}
\end{panel}

% --------------------------------------------------------- 5  Key insights ---
\begin{panel}{5}{Key Insights}
  \insight{1}{Carrying \mono{h} forward is not what matters.}{Every GRU arm
    does it identically, including the ones that fail. What separates them is
    whether the \textbf{gradient} reaches back to the observation that filled
    \mono{h}, and reaching past 8 adds nothing.}
  \vspace{6mm}

  \insight{2}{What must fit inside \Lw{} is the \textbf{gap}, not the
    episode.}{The gap runs from the last sighting of the cue to the choice at
    the fork. A gap of at most 8 is attainable in \textbf{62\,\%} of mazes, one
    of at most 4 in only \textbf{26\,\%}: cue and decision share a chunk in
    16\,\% of the \Leq{8} agent's episodes and in \textbf{0 of 50} of the
    \Leq{4} agent's.}
  \vspace{6mm}

  \insight{3}{The failing arms are not partially remembering.}{At 7.0 steps
    the \Leq{4} arm dashes straight to the fork and always picks the same side,
    exactly 25/50 here. Its across-seed std of 0.000 is \textbf{arithmetic, not
    convergence}.}
  \vspace{6mm}

  \insight{4}{The reach costs memory, not time.}{Full BPTT is the
    \textbf{fastest} GRU arm (1.3\,h against 2.6\,h at \Leq{1}) and the
    earliest (0.95 success at a median of 370 iterations against 640 for
    \Leq{8}): halving \Lw{} doubles the padded, launch-bound sequences. What it
    pays is VRAM, minibatch 512 against 4096.}
  \vspace{7mm}

  \begin{callout}
    {\pbodys\color{luhblue}\textbf{Recommendation.} Use full BPTT, with
     \Leq{8} as the fallback on a smaller GPU. Below 8 you do not get a cheaper
     solution, you get the MLP's guessing policy at GRU prices.\par}
  \end{callout}
\end{panel}

\end{minipage}
